body.cap: The 'Neuroid' platform showcased by Nation A at CES Unveiled. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Nation A, led by CEO Yoo Su-yeon, participated in the global media event 'CES Unveiled' on January 7th, preceding the official start of CES 2024 in Las Vegas. Since October of the previous year, the company has been operating 'Neuroid,' a 3D and 4D data creation SaaS platform. Neuroid's service creates motion data from user-entered text and offers it to users as AR (Augmented Reality), VR (Virtual Reality), and 3D assets. It reached a million users milestone within a month of its launch.

A key advantage of Neuroid is the ability to quickly produce the intended motion data in various forms from just text input. This capability can reduce workforce requirements in related industries, enhancing operational efficiency and maximizing cost-effectiveness. It also lowers the barrier to high-quality content creation for general consumers using the platform.

Before the opening of CES 2024, Nation A participated in CES Unveiled, targeting global media as part of its comprehensive global promotion strategy. CEO Yoo Su-yeon commented, “Since our founding, we have been reaching out to customers across all cultural realms worldwide, and our participation in CES 2024 and Unveiled is a step to accelerate achieving this goal.”

body.cap: Nation A representatives interacting with the international press at CES Unveiled. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: CEO Yoo stated, “Neuroid, a B2C service that supports easy and fast 3D content creation, has garnered significant interest from influencers of various nationalities at the event. Their positive responses pave the way for potential future collaborations.”

The Consumer Technology Association (CTA), host of CES, the world's largest IT exhibition, provides a platform in Las Vegas each January to showcase global consumer electronics trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been reporting CES news worldwide since 2006, highlighting products, companies, and technologies with the 'BEST OF CES' and 'BEST OF MADE IN KOREA' awards programs. They also discuss issues in the field from the CES scene through 'AVING LIVE.'

The CES 2024 Seoul pavilion, operating on its most enormous scale since Seoul's first CES participation in 2020, is a joint effort of 13 organizations, including SBA, Seoul Bio Hub, Campus Town, AI Yangjae Hub, Gwanak District, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, Konkuk University, and Kyung Hee University. This collaborative pavilion marks a significant step in Seoul's ambition to become a startup hub, and among its participating companies, 17 received innovation awards, evidencing their excellence. The pavilion also includes 85 supporters in a significant collaboration between companies, institutions, and industry-academia cooperation.
